narrative.overview: This is the read-out for a piece of equipment, not an app being sold. Surfaces are quiet white under a faint cool daylight canvas; structure is drawn with hairlines, not boxes-in-boxes; every EPC, reader ID, and timestamp is set in monospace so codes read like measurements. One cerulean carries identity and intent. Alarm red stays in a locked drawer and only appears when a watched tag is actually detected. The register is product: the design serves the task and then disappears.
keyCharacteristics: Light, pure-white surfaces on a faint cool canvas; depth from hairlines, not shadow.
One cerulean for identity; alarm red rationed to genuine alarm states only.
Monospace for every machine value (EPC, reader, timestamp, counts).
Calm density: comfortable, scannable rows, never a wall of gray.
State is never color-only: color + icon + text, always.

rules.name: The Locked-Drawer Rule
rules.body: Signal Red is forbidden as decoration. It appears only where a real watched tag has been detected: alarm rows, the active-alarm banner, the alarm status chip and its count. If red is on screen, something is actually wrong.

rules.name: The Whisper Tint Rule
rules.body: Status is a wash-tinted chip with dark ink and a colored dot, not a saturated block. Saturated fills are reserved for the single most urgent affordance on a screen.

rules.name: The Machine-Value Rule
rules.body: Anything the hardware produces (EPC, reader ID, timestamp, count) is set in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures. Human language stays in Plex Sans.

rules.name: The Two-Step Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy comes from at most two visible weights (400 and 600) plus scale. No light-weight body, no third typeface.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-Floating Rule
rules.body: A surface that is part of the layout gets a hairline and no shadow. A surface that floats above the layout gets a shadow and no heavy border.

dos: Do keep Signal Red in the locked drawer: alarm rows, alarm chip, live-alarm banner, alarm count. Nowhere else.
Do set every EPC, reader ID, timestamp, and count in IBM Plex Mono with tabular figures.
Do pair every status with an icon and a text label; color is the third signal, never the only one.
Do draw structure with hairlines and the canvas/surface step; keep resting surfaces flat.
Do keep Ink Muted (#5c646b) as the lightest text on screen; bump toward Ink if a value matters.
Do give the data table the most care: alignment, mono columns, a teaching empty state, a visible focus and keyboard path.
donts: Don't ship the stock PrimeNG Aura theme; override the tokens so nothing reads as a sample app.
Don't build a generic AI dashboard: no gradient stat cards, no oversized hero metric, no decorative charts, no identical icon-card grid.
Don't drift toward legacy ERP: no dense gray forms, no toolbar thickets, no borders-inside-borders.
Don't add flashy or playful flourishes: no gamified color, no bounce/elastic motion, no animation that doesn't convey state.
Don't use a border-left/border-right colored stripe as an accent on rows, cards, or alerts.
Don't use gradient text, decorative glassmorphism, or a saturated status fill where a wash tint will do.
Don't signal any state by color alone, and never animate the alarm emphasis as the only cue (respect prefers-reduced-motion).
